newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air Canada ups ex-Germany cargo rates 5-10pc.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada ups ex-Germany cargo rates 5-10pc.

text.p: Air Canada said it will raise ex-Germany cargo rates by five to ten percent from April 1.
Konrad Bossdorf, cargo manager Germany and northern Europe, said the rise was justified by good demand for North America at present.
"Business is pretty strong at the moment. The market seems to be very strong at present and the dollar is boosting exports," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Bossdorf said that German cargo for Montreal would have to go via Toronto or Halifax this summer since planned flights to the Quebec capital have been cancelled.
Non-stop flights from Dorval International airport to Frankfurt and Tel Aviv due to start in June have been cancelled due to problems consolidating international and domestic services at the airport.
Air Canada would expand cargo capacity from Germany to North America this summer, Bossdorf said.
The Calgary-Frankfurt route would be upgraded to an Airbus A340 from a Boeing B767-300.
Next winter, Air Canada and partner Lufthansa were considering operating four combi aircraft flights a week between Germany and Canada under a blocked space agreement, he added.
